JC-A00 R6 (G1/G2): sensor runtime state completeness and atomic import. G1 verifies the FULL dynamic pointing state (pointing_mode + desired_target_id + az/el) survives restore so a slowly moving target keeps being tracked for 130 ticks with zero divergence (an angle-only save freezes tracking). G2 verifies two-phase atomic import (optical / TWS / radar / authority metadata are all validated before ANY layer commits) and strict rejection of: fractional or unknown versions, out-of-range angles, illegal pointing modes, negative times, fractional scan_index, malformed channel fields, and missing TWS/radar sub-state - each rejection must leave every child clock unchanged.

cases.purpose: JC-B03P (P0): concrete theater proposal content spec. Validates objective references/required fields/military attributes, fleet-pool points budget vs two tactically different formations, explicit protection objectives (civilian infrastructure must not be an attack/victory target), five terminal outcomes with timeout not producing victory, three coordination request/response templates, and event traces with unique expected terminal states, monotonic time, and idempotent adjudication (disabled-but-unreported stays pending_report; single EW or a still-engaging target never counts as permanent disable). Content logic only - it does not implement a runtime adjudicator and the traces are NOT real battle reports.

JC-B00 (K0): joint-campaign multi-fleet / command / intel contract. Validates structure, reference integrity, permission separation (faction vs controller vs intel_owner vs ROE), deployment lifecycle single-step with idempotent request ids, observation observed_t<=received_t with explicit owner/path/delay, explicit shooter within the commanding domain (never falls back to flagship), resource ledgers that cannot reference another ship, t->kg conversion exactly once, and reversible JSON roundtrip. Semantic validator only (not a full JSON Schema engine); it does not simulate AI or claim a real fleet is deployed.

DS-A-06: comms read-back recovery for a real HUD session. send_comms records a versioned outcome (ok/reason/mode/delivery_id/path/latency/relay/arrive_t/sent_t); replay re-executes each op and compares item by item, so an ORIGINAL failure (e.g. no_route) stays a failure instead of becoming a recovery error while a real divergence (success->failure, or mismatched reason/id/path/latency) is rejected with comms_replay_diverged. Covers LD direct, LR relay, queued and immediate deliveries with exactly-once delivery after restore, and legacy logs without outcomes are labelled legacy_unverified per the A-04 version rules.

DS-A-05: SensorService runtime persistence and continuation. EMCON/radar toggled away from the seed, optical+IR channels advanced past the initial state, then memory+real-file roundtrip: controls, clock, selected target, backend channel state (status/progress/samples), obs/evidence/event allocators and dedup keys must survive; static mounts/targets and provider objects are NOT persisted and are rebuilt/re-injected (same-tick geometry, bary_rot); restored history is not replayed into TrackTable; EMCON behaviour persists (no radar emissions while on, output resumes when off); negatives carry explicit reasons; old saves without the section are labelled as not having runtime state.

DS-A-04: legacy save migration and dedup beyond the 1000-event ring buffer. Real I3 fixtures with documented provenance; shape A (no bus section) and shape B (legacy bus.seq/events only) must merge the replay used-id set UNION the visible history ids (never a tail replacement), so an early explicit id evicted from the visible ring is still rejected on re-publish; high watermark never goes backwards; new seq continues monotonically and auto ids never collide; partial recovery and unrecoverable sensor state are labelled honestly; corrupt/unknown/illegal inputs are rejected explicitly instead of silently starting a new simulation.

DS-A-03: EventBus versioned state export/import. History restore is an IMPORT (no publish, no dispatch, subscribers called 0 times); numeric JSON contract uses value semantics (finite integral, 0..2^53-1, event seq >=1, strictly increasing) while restored runtime seq/allocator MUST be real GDScript ints; full used-id set preserved past MAX_EVENTS=1000; allocator never collides with used evt-* ids; invalid seq/version/ordering rejected atomically (bus state unchanged); real-file session save->load->continue produces identical seq/allocator/ids.

DS-A-02: frame/epoch and consumer time sources. Scenario UTC epoch is the single calendar source (exactly consistent with the integer epoch label); the CR3BP phase basis is explicitly separated and never replaced by UTC seconds; every physics-chain consumer declares frame=bary_rot with a source; L1 seed conversion happens exactly once and is marked applied/source; the central frame converter roundtrips in double precision near origin and at EML1 large coordinates; save/load preserves epoch/relative time/frame/source; invalid UTC / unknown frame / legacy seed are explicit (no fabricated calendar date).

DS-A-01: same-commit integration acceptance of the P17/P19/P20 chain. No-noise scalar geometry (provider vs independent double math), observer AND target moved separately via the authorized physics API, uncertainty observation kept as measurement (not pulled to truth), production error params traced from the real radar/optical/IR backend records, per-consumer source/frame/t table, failure/degradation reasons with advisory-vs-unavailable geometry labelling (invalid geometry must stop routing), and player-visibility checks.
